faqs.question: Do I need the WhatsApp Business app to use TopEdge AI?
faqs.answer: No. TopEdge AI runs on the WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API), which is a different product from the WhatsApp Business phone app. You can keep using the app on a different number, or enable coexistence on the same number if your WhatsApp Business Account supports it.

faqs.question: Can I use TopEdge AI without Shopify?
faqs.answer: The inbox, Flow Builder, templates, campaigns and the AI brain all work without Shopify. Order journeys, cart recovery, product catalogue and store economics need the Shopify connection, because those read order and checkout data from your store.

faqs.question: How long does setup take?
faqs.answer: About 30 minutes of setup. Meta verification and template review are the wait. That assumes you already have a WhatsApp Business Account on Meta. Many templates clear in minutes and most within a day. Meta guarantees no time.

articles.title: Quickstart: WhatsApp automation for Shopify
articles.description: Go live with TopEdge AI in about 30 minutes: connect Shopify and WhatsApp, approve an order template, publish one journey and send yourself a test message.
articles.lead: Connect your store, get one template approved and send yourself a real order message. About 30 minutes, plus Meta’s review time.

faqs.question: Why has my test WhatsApp message not arrived?
faqs.answer: Check four things in order: the journey is Published rather than Draft, the template it uses shows Approved, the order carries a phone number in international format, and WhatsApp still shows Connected. The order detail page records a skip reason that names which of these failed.

faqs.question: Can I test without placing a real order?
faqs.answer: Yes for conversations, Flow Builder has a simulator that walks menus and buttons without messaging anyone. Order journeys need a real Shopify order to trigger, so most merchants place a small test order and cancel or refund it afterwards.

faqs.question: Do I need a new phone number for WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but the number cannot be actively registered in the WhatsApp Business app unless your WhatsApp Business Account has coexistence enabled. Many merchants use a dedicated number for automation and keep their existing one for manual chats.

A WhatsApp Business Account on the Cloud API, with a phone number that is **not** currently active in the WhatsApp Business app (or with coexistence enabled).
Admin rights in Meta Business Manager, so you can approve the connection and submit templates.
A second phone you can message from: a business number cannot message itself.

articles.title: Connect WhatsApp Cloud API to TopEdge AI
articles.description: Connect your WhatsApp Business Account to TopEdge AI: embedded Meta signup, the messages webhook, permanent access tokens, and how to fix a disconnected channel.
articles.lead: Link your WhatsApp Business number so TopEdge AI can send messages and receive replies.

faqs.question: Why is my WhatsApp inbox empty even though the channel is connected?
faqs.answer: Connection and the message subscription are separate. TopEdge AI can send as soon as the token is valid, but replies only arrive once TopEdge AI is subscribed to your messages. Embedded signup does this for you; if the inbox stays empty, reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp.

faqs.question: What kind of WhatsApp access token should I use?
faqs.answer: A System User token with the whatsapp_business_messaging permission. The token offered on the Meta developer dashboard is a temporary test token that expires in roughly 24 hours, which makes the channel appear to break by itself the next day.

faqs.question: Can I keep using the WhatsApp Business app on the same number?
faqs.answer: Only if coexistence is enabled on your WhatsApp Business Account. Otherwise a number can be registered either on the Cloud API or in the WhatsApp Business app, not both, and embedded signup will report that the number is already in use.

blocks.text: Connect from **Settings → WhatsApp** using Meta's embedded signup. It creates the access token and subscribes TopEdge AI to your messages for you. Send yourself a test message afterwards to confirm replies reach the inbox.

items: A WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) in Meta Business Manager, and admin rights on it.
A phone number that can receive an SMS or call to verify, and that is not actively registered in the WhatsApp Business app.
A verified business on Meta if you want to raise your messaging limits beyond the starting tier.

blocks.text: Connect with embedded signup (recommended)

blocks.alt: Settings channels list with the WhatsApp card and its Connect button

blocks.text: Embedded signup runs Meta’s own flow inside the dashboard, so you never handle a token yourself. In one pass it:

items: **Creates or selects** your WhatsApp Business Account (WABA).
**Registers** the phone number.
**Subscribes** TopEdge AI to the account.
**Stores** a long-lived access token.

blocks.howToName: Connect a WhatsApp Business Account to TopEdge AI

steps.title: Open WhatsApp connections
steps.body: Settings → WhatsApp → **Connect**.

steps.title: Sign in to Meta
steps.body: Use the Facebook account that administers your business. A personal account with no Business Manager access cannot finish this.

steps.title: Pick or create the WhatsApp Business Account
steps.body: Choose the WABA that owns the number you want to send from. A second WABA for the same business is a common reason templates later seem to go missing.

steps.title: Add and verify the phone number
steps.body: Enter the number, choose SMS or voice, and type the code. Verified numbers show green in Meta.

steps.title: Finish and return to TopEdge AI
steps.body: The card should read **Connected**, with the phone number and WhatsApp Business Account it uses.

steps.title: Send yourself a test
steps.body: Message your business number from a personal phone. The thread should appear in Chats within seconds.
steps.note: Embedded signup subscribes TopEdge AI to your messages, so there is no webhook to set up.

blocks.text: Manual credentials (advanced)
Manual credentials are hidden in the dashboard and only needed when embedded signup cannot finish, for example on an agency-managed WABA.
**Contact TopEdge AI support** to switch it on. You will need four values from the Meta developer console: the Phone Number ID, the WABA ID, an access token and your Meta App ID.

blocks.title: Temporary tokens expire in about 24 hours
blocks.body: The token on the Meta developer dashboard is a test token, so a channel that dies after a day almost always used one. Production needs a **System User** token with the `whatsapp_business_messaging` permission, which does not expire.

The account that owns your numbers and templates. Templates are scoped to this, which is why connecting the wrong WABA makes your template library look empty.
Authorises TopEdge AI to call Meta on your behalf. Use a System User token in production.
A shared secret Meta echoes back when it first calls your webhook URL, proving the endpoint is yours.

blocks.text: If something goes wrong

cases.symptom: Amber "WhatsApp disconnected" bar across every page
fixes: Open Settings → WhatsApp and reconnect. If you are on manual credentials, paste a fresh permanent System User token.
A token that stopped working overnight was almost certainly a 24-hour test token.
Confirm the number has not been disconnected or migrated inside Meta Business Manager.
Reconnect, then send a test message to confirm inbound still arrives.

cases.symptom: Connection succeeds but the inbox stays empty
fixes: Reconnect from Settings → WhatsApp so embedded signup re-subscribes TopEdge AI to your messages. Sending works without it, receiving does not.
Message from a personal phone. A business number cannot message itself.
Confirm a flow is Published in [Flow Builder](/docs/reference/flow-builder), otherwise inbound messages arrive with no automated reply.

cases.symptom: Embedded signup says the phone number is already in use
fixes: The number is registered in the WhatsApp Business app. Either delete that account or enable coexistence on your WABA.
Check for a second Cloud API app already claiming the number in Meta Business Manager.
As a last resort, verify a different number and keep the old one for manual chats.

cases.symptom: Template library is empty after connecting
fixes: You are almost certainly connected to a different WhatsApp Business Account than the one holding your templates.
Check which WABA the connection names, and compare it with the account in Meta Business Manager.
Reconnect against the correct WABA, then use **Sync from Meta** in Meta Manager.

articles.title: Connect Shopify to TopEdge AI
articles.description: Install the TopEdge AI Shopify app, understand the permissions it asks for, verify that orders sync, and fix a store stuck on Reconnect.
articles.lead: Install the TopEdge AI app on your store so orders, products and abandoned checkouts sync.

faqs.question: Does TopEdge AI edit my Shopify theme?
faqs.answer: No. Storefront tracking installs through Shopify app embeds and the web pixel extension, both of which are managed in the theme editor and removed cleanly when you disable them. TopEdge AI reads your theme only to check whether the opt-in embed is enabled.

faqs.question: Why does Shopify ask me to reconnect?
faqs.answer: Shopify requires a fresh approval whenever an app starts using a capability you have not already granted. Until you approve it, the features relying on that capability stop working: missing shipped and delivered messages are the usual symptom.

faqs.question: Can I connect more than one Shopify store?
faqs.answer: Each workspace binds to one Shopify store, so a second store needs its own workspace. Connecting a different store to an existing workspace releases the previous binding, which is why test stores should be disconnected before you connect the real one.

blocks.text: Connect from **Settings → Shopify**, or open TopEdge AI from Shopify admin. You approve the app’s permissions once in Shopify, and orders start syncing within a minute or two. You never type your store domain; the install is always approved inside Shopify.

items: Shopify admin or staff access with permission to install apps.
A store on a plan that allows app installs (development stores are fine for testing).
If you also use a third-party checkout, access to that provider’s dashboard for the webhook step.

blocks.alt: Shopify connect window showing the connected store and its list of approved permissions

steps.title: Start the connect flow
steps.body: **Settings → Shopify → Connect**. You can also start from **Shopify admin → Apps → TopEdge AI**, which brings you back to the dashboard afterwards.

steps.title: Approve the permissions in Shopify
steps.body: Shopify shows the full permission list. Approve all of it, because a partial grant breaks specific features silently instead of disabling them visibly.
steps.note: See [what each permission is for](#permissions) below.

steps.title: Wait for webhooks to register
steps.body: TopEdge AI subscribes to the order, fulfilment, checkout and app-lifecycle webhooks it needs. This happens automatically right after install.

steps.title: Verify orders sync
steps.body: Open **Orders** and press **Sync**. Live orders should appear within one to two minutes.

steps.title: Install storefront tracking
steps.body: Only needed for cart recovery and browse events. **Website tracking** installs the theme embed, web pixel and checkout extension; see [Abandoned carts and tracking](/docs/reference/store-growth).

blocks.alt: Orders table listing real Shopify orders after a sync
blocks.caption: After a Sync, Orders lists your real store orders.

blocks.text: What the permissions are for

Shopify asks you to approve everything at once, so here is what each group unlocks. TopEdge AI writes to your store only for the actions listed, such as tagging an order, setting stock or creating a payment link.

rows: Order journeys and triggers, commerce analytics, and the order actions you take from the inbox: tag, cancel, mark paid.
Product catalogue for flows and message templates, stock levels, and setting quantities from the Stock screen.
Audience CRM, identity matching by phone number, and abandoned checkout detection for cart recovery.
Shipped and delivered journeys, tracking numbers, and creating fulfilments from the Orders screen.
COD → prepaid payment links and cart recovery invoices, plus issuing recovery discount codes.
The storefront web pixel that captures carts and browse events.
Detecting whether the TopEdge AI opt-in app embed is enabled on your live theme. TopEdge AI never edits theme files.
Session and payout figures shown in Insights. Read-only, and never used to move money.

blocks.body: When the app starts using a new Shopify capability, your store shows a **Reconnect** prompt. Approving it re-grants the full set; until then the new feature stays off, which is why something can seem to stop after an update.

items: The Shopify card reads **Connected** and shows your store domain.
Orders lists real orders after a Sync.
Product search returns your catalogue.
For cart recovery: **Website tracking** shows **Installed** with a recent last event.

blocks.text: If something goes wrong

cases.symptom: Shopify card shows Reconnect, or fulfilments are missing
fixes: Settings → Shopify → **Reconnect** and approve the full permission list again.
Open Orders → **Sync** and wait a couple of minutes.
Missing shipped or delivered messages are nearly always missing fulfilment permissions: reconnecting fixes it.

cases.symptom: Orders table stays empty after connecting
fixes: Press **Sync** on the Orders screen; the first load is a backfill, not a webhook.
Confirm the connected store domain is the store you are actually looking at in Shopify admin.
If you connected several stores while testing, make sure this workspace owns the right one.

cases.symptom: Dashboard numbers do not match Shopify analytics
fixes: Compare the same date range and the same definition: Shopify’s total sales includes shipping and tax, while store economics reports net of cost.
Press Sync to backfill any orders that arrived while the connection was down.
Orders placed before you connected are backfilled, but only for the window the sync covers.

cases.symptom: You uninstalled from Shopify but TopEdge AI still shows Connected
fixes: Reload the dashboard: connection state is cached briefly.
If it persists, press Reconnect and then disconnect cleanly from Settings.
Uninstalling in Shopify revokes the token, so no further data moves either way regardless of what the card says.

articles.title: Go-live checklist before real customers
articles.description: The checks to run before TopEdge AI messages real customers: connections, approved templates, published journeys, consent, tracking and a live end-to-end test.
articles.lead: Run through this list once before real customers start getting messages.

faqs.question: What is the most common reason a WhatsApp automation does not send?
faqs.answer: A journey left in Draft. Publishing is a separate action from saving, and a saved draft looks complete in the editor while sending nothing. The second most common reason is a template that is still pending Meta approval.

faqs.question: Do order confirmations need marketing consent?
faqs.answer: No. Order, shipping and delivery updates are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing opt-in. Promotional broadcasts are different and do need recorded consent from the contact.

blocks.text: Before going live, confirm both channels are connected and every template your journeys use is **Approved**. Each journey you expect to run must be **Published**, and marketing should target only contacts with recorded consent. Then run one real end-to-end test on a real phone.
Connections

blocks.alt: Settings with the WhatsApp and Shopify cards showing their connection state

items: Shopify shows **Connected** with the correct store domain.
WhatsApp shows **Connected** with the number you want customers to see.
A test message from your phone shows up in Chats.
Your WhatsApp token is a permanent System User token, not a 24-hour test token.
Gmail is connected if any journey or campaign sends email.

blocks.text: Templates

blocks.alt: Meta Manager template library listing templates with their approval status

items: Every template referenced by a published journey shows **Approved**.
Order and shipping templates are in the **Utility** category and contain no promotional language.
Promotional templates are in the **Marketing** category.
Variables are mapped: a template with unmapped variables sends with blanks or fails outright.
The preview in the dashboard matches what you want the customer to receive.

blocks.title: Approved at send time, not at publish time
blocks.body: Meta can pause or disable a template after approval if quality drops. A journey that worked last week can then start skipping sends with no change on your side; the skip reason on the order says so.

blocks.text: Automations

blocks.alt: Journeys hub listing order and cart automations

marks.label: On means the journey is sending

items: Each journey you expect to run shows **Published**. Draft journeys never send.
The trigger on each journey matches the event you think it does: order confirmation is the **order placed** trigger.
Trigger filters are deliberate. All rules combine with AND, so two narrow rules can exclude everyone.
Wait timings are what you intend: the first cart reminder is minutes, not instant.
Your main flow is Published in Flow Builder, so replies get an answer.

items: Marketing broadcasts target only contacts with recorded opt-in.
No purchased or scraped phone lists are loaded into Audience.
Opt-in tools carry consent wording that names WhatsApp marketing explicitly.
STOP handling is understood: it opts the contact out of marketing automatically.
Order and shipping updates use Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent.

items: **Website tracking** shows **Installed** with a recent last event.
The TopEdge AI opt-in app embed is enabled on your **live** theme, not a preview theme.
A test abandoned checkout produced a cart row **with a phone number**.
If you use a third-party checkout, its webhook is configured and tested.

steps.body: Use a number you control, in international format. Check the WhatsApp message reads correctly on the phone, not just in the dashboard preview.

steps.body: Enter your phone at checkout and leave. Confirm the cart shows under abandoned carts with the phone filled in, then wait for the first reminder.

steps.body: Press **Reply myself** on the thread and send a free-form reply. Then press **Give back to bot** and confirm automation resumes on your next message.

steps.body: Complete the abandoned checkout. Confirm the cart is marked recovered with revenue attributed.

articles.title: Set up WhatsApp abandoned cart recovery
articles.description: Turn on WhatsApp abandoned cart recovery for your Shopify store: check carts arrive with a phone number, approve three templates and publish the journey.
articles.h1: How to turn on abandoned cart recovery
articles.lead: Send a WhatsApp reminder when a shopper leaves checkout without paying. Setup takes about 20 minutes once your templates are approved.

faqs.question: How soon should the first abandoned cart message go out?
faqs.answer: About 25 minutes after the shopper leaves. That is the default **Wait before enroll** on the Cart recovery playbook. Sending at once chases people who only switched tabs, and waiting several hours loses the ones still deciding.

faqs.question: Why is my abandoned cart missing a phone number?
faqs.answer: The shopper left before typing one, or tracking is not capturing it. Adding to cart alone never gives a phone number. Check **Website tracking** shows a recent event and that the TopEdge AI app embed is on in your live theme.

faqs.question: How many cart recovery messages should I send?
faqs.answer: Three: a reminder, a message that answers common doubts, and a final nudge. More than three costs more in Meta charges and annoyed customers than it brings back.

faqs.question: Should I offer a discount in the first message?
faqs.answer: No. Most recovered carts come back without one. Keep any discount for the third reminder, so you do not pay for sales you would have made anyway.

blocks.text: Open **Journeys**, start from the **Cart recovery** playbook, pick an approved WhatsApp template for each of its three messages, then press **Publish**. The first reminder goes out 25 minutes after the cart is abandoned. Only carts with a phone number get a message.

items: Shopify and WhatsApp are connected: [Connect Shopify](/docs/connect-shopify), [Connect WhatsApp](/docs/connect-whatsapp).
A second phone, or a number that is not your business number, for testing.
A product in your store you can add to cart.

blocks.text: How it works

A shopper types their phone number at checkout and leaves. TopEdge AI saves that as an abandoned cart, waits, then sends up to three reminders. If the shopper orders at any point, the remaining reminders are cancelled.

blocks.name: cart-recovery-ladder
blocks.title: The three reminders
blocks.caption: These are the default waits in the Cart recovery playbook. You can change each one.

blocks.text: Step 1: Check that carts arrive with a phone number
Do this first. A cart without a phone number cannot be messaged, however good the journey is.

steps.title: Open Website tracking
steps.body: In the sidebar, under **Store**, click **Website tracking**. The chip at the top should read **Installed** or **Live** with a recent last-event time.
steps.note: No recent event? Press **Reconnect pixel** and approve it in Shopify.
steps.alt: Website tracking screen with the tracking status chip and the Reconnect pixel button at the top

marks.label: Status and the time of the last event

steps.title: Turn on the app embed in your live theme
steps.body: In Shopify admin go to **Online Store → Themes → Customize** on your **live** theme. Open **App embeds**, switch on the TopEdge AI embeds and press **Save**.
steps.note: It must be the published theme. A preview or duplicate theme does not count.

steps.title: Abandon a test checkout
steps.body: Open your store in an incognito window. Add a product to the cart, go to checkout, type a real phone number, then close the tab without paying.

steps.title: Find your test cart
steps.body: Back in TopEdge AI, open **Abandoned carts**. Your cart should appear within a few minutes, with the phone number under the customer name.
steps.alt: Abandoned carts list showing each cart with the customer phone number, cart value and status

marks.label: A phone number under the customer name

blocks.title: No phone number, no message
blocks.body: If the cart shows up without a phone number, fix tracking before you touch the journey. See [If it is not working](#troubleshooting).

blocks.text: Step 2: Get three templates approved
WhatsApp only lets you send messages that Meta has approved. Cart recovery uses three, one per reminder.

steps.title: Open your templates
steps.body: In the sidebar click **Meta Manager**. Check whether three cart recovery templates already show **Approved**.
steps.alt: WhatsApp templates list in Meta Manager with a status column showing Approved, In review and Rejected

marks.label: **Create Meta template** starts a new one

steps.title: Create them if they are missing
steps.body: Open the **Blueprints** tab and use the cart recovery set. Each template comes with the product image, the customer’s name and a button back to checkout already filled in. Submit all three.
steps.note: Building one by hand? Follow [Create a WhatsApp template](/docs/guides/create-whatsapp-template).

steps.title: Wait for Approved
steps.body: Meta usually answers within minutes, sometimes up to a day. Carry on once all three read **Approved**.

blocks.caption: What each reminder is for
rows: 25 minutes after the cart is abandoned
Show what they left, with one button back to checkout. No discount.
Answer the usual doubts: delivery time, returns, COD.
A last nudge. If you offer a discount, offer it here.

Third-party checkout apps

articles.title: Confirm COD orders on WhatsApp to cut RTO
articles.description: Confirm cash-on-delivery orders over WhatsApp with button replies, cancel the ones nobody confirms, and offer a prepaid switch to reduce return-to-origin losses.
articles.h1: How to confirm COD orders on WhatsApp
articles.lead: Ask every cash-on-delivery customer to confirm with one tap before you ship, and cancel the orders nobody wants.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp COD confirmation actually reduce RTO?
faqs.answer: It reduces the share of RTO caused by unintended and duplicate orders, which is the largest removable chunk. It cannot fix RTO caused by delivery failures, wrong addresses or buyer remorse after dispatch. Measure your own before-and-after rather than trusting a headline number.

faqs.question: When should the COD confirmation message be sent?
faqs.answer: Five to fifteen minutes after the order. The customer still remembers placing it, and you are well ahead of dispatch. Sending instantly feels automated and jumpy; waiting hours means the order may already be packed.

faqs.question: What should I do when a customer never confirms?
faqs.answer: Send exactly one follow-up, then apply your own rule. Many stores hold high-value unconfirmed COD orders for a phone call and dispatch low-value ones anyway, because the shipping cost of being wrong is smaller than the lost sale.

faqs.question: Do I need a separate template for COD confirmation?
faqs.answer: Yes. It needs quick-reply buttons so the customer can answer with one tap, and the body has to read as a transactional order confirmation to pass review as a Utility template. Your order confirmation template will not have the buttons.

blocks.text: Publish a journey on the **order placed** trigger, filtered to COD, that sends an approved template with Confirm and Cancel buttons within minutes. Confirmed orders go to dispatch and silent ones get one follow-up. On Growth plans and above you can also offer a prepaid payment link that replaces the COD order with a paid one.

items: Shopify and WhatsApp connected, with orders syncing.
An approved template with quick-reply buttons: see [Message templates](/docs/platform/message-templates).
For the prepaid switch: a plan that includes COD → prepaid, and Shopify permission to create draft orders.
A COD order you can place as a test.

blocks.text: Why confirmation works
A COD order costs nothing to place, so it attracts impulse, duplicate and mistaken orders. You usually find out at the door, after paying for shipping both ways.
One tap of confirmation moves that discovery to before dispatch, where cancelling is almost free.

rows: Dispatch normally. Tag the order as confirmed so your warehouse can see it.
Cancel in Shopify before dispatch. You just saved both legs of shipping.
The thread is in [Chats](/docs/reference/live-chat) with the order beside it: answer and confirm manually.
Send one follow-up. After that, decide by your own risk rules: hold, call, or dispatch anyway.

blocks.howToName: Set up WhatsApp COD order confirmation on Shopify

steps.title: Start from the COD confirmation playbook
steps.body: Open **Journeys**, click **Browse playbooks** and pick **COD confirmation**. It creates a journey on the **Order placed** trigger with the confirm and cancel paths in place.
steps.note: There is no separate "order confirmed" trigger. Order placed is the one to use.
steps.alt: Browse playbooks dialog with the COD confirmation and COD to prepaid playbooks

steps.title: Filter to COD only
steps.body: In the trigger setup, add a **payment method** rule set to COD. Without it, prepaid customers are asked to confirm orders they already paid for.

steps.title: Add a short wait
steps.body: Five to fifteen minutes. The customer has left your site, but the message is clearly about the order they just placed.

steps.title: Send the confirmation template
steps.body: Map an approved template with Confirm and Cancel quick replies. TopEdge AI sets the step to wait for a button tap rather than free text.

steps.title: Branch on the answer (Growth and above)
steps.body: A conditional split sends confirmed and cancelled down different paths: tag and dispatch on one, cancel and notify on the other.
steps.note: On Launch, skip the branch and handle non-responders from the Orders screen instead.

steps.title: Add a follow-up for silence
steps.body: Add a second wait of a few hours, then one more message. Stop there, because more than two asks reads as harassment.

steps.title: Publish and place a test COD order
steps.body: Use your own phone: tap Confirm and check the order records it. Then place another and tap Cancel.

blocks.text: Offering the prepaid switch
The strongest version of this flow offers to convert, not just confirm. A small incentive to pay now turns your riskiest orders into your safest, because prepaid orders almost never return to origin.

blocks.name: cod-prepaid-switch
blocks.title: What happens when a customer chooses to prepay
blocks.caption: Shopify voids the COD order and creates a paid one, so expect two order records for one purchase.

blocks.title: Two order records, one sale
blocks.body: A converted order appears twice in Shopify: the voided COD order and the new paid one. TopEdge AI recognises the replacement, so it is not counted twice against your order allowance, in revenue attribution, or in your COD share.

rows: Enough to beat the customer’s inertia, well below your RTO cost per order. Free shipping or a small flat discount is typical.
In the confirmation message itself, as the alternative to confirming COD. A separate later message converts far less.
What happens to the COD order
It is voided when the payment succeeds. The new paid order carries a tag identifying it as a conversion.
Nothing breaks. The original COD order stands and your normal flow continues.

items: A test COD order produces a confirmation message with working buttons.
A prepaid test order does **not** receive the confirmation.
Tapping Confirm is recorded against the order.
Tapping Cancel routes down the cancel path, if you built one.
A prepaid payment link opens a valid Shopify checkout for the right amount.

blocks.text: If confirmation is not working

cases.symptom: Prepaid customers are getting the COD confirmation
fixes: Add the **payment method = COD** filter to the trigger. Without it, order placed matches every order.
Republish after editing the trigger: a live journey keeps the trigger it was published with.

cases.symptom: Buttons appear but taps do nothing
fixes: The template must use quick-reply buttons, not a URL button.
Send a test message first: if it reaches Chats, button taps will reach TopEdge AI too.
Check no agent pressed **Reply myself** on the thread in Chats; that pauses automation.

cases.symptom: The COD → prepaid node is locked
fixes: It is a Growth-and-above feature. See [plan limits](/docs/platform/limits-and-quotas).
Already-published journeys keep running after a downgrade, but you cannot edit or create them.

cases.symptom: A converted order looks like two orders
fixes: That is Shopify’s behaviour: the COD order is voided and a paid one created.
TopEdge AI skips the replacement for order counting, revenue and re-enrolment, so you are not billed or messaged twice.
If a replacement did get a second message, the conversion tag was stripped from the order in Shopify.

articles.title: Send Shopify order updates on WhatsApp

articles.h1: How to send order updates on WhatsApp
articles.lead: Send confirmed, shipped and delivered messages automatically. This is the safest automation to start with.

faqs.question: Which trigger should I use for a Shopify order confirmation?
faqs.answer: The order placed trigger. An order being placed is the confirmation event, and there is no separate order confirmed trigger. Expecting one is the most common reason a confirmation journey is built but never fires.

faqs.question: Do order status messages need marketing opt-in?
faqs.answer: No. They are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent. That is exactly why they are the safest automation to start with: but it also means they must contain no promotional language at all.

faqs.question: Why are my shipped and delivered messages not sending?
faqs.answer: Almost always missing fulfilment permissions on the Shopify connection. Order confirmations only need order access, so confirmations keep working while shipping messages silently do nothing. Reconnect Shopify and approve the full permission list.

blocks.text: Publish one journey per stage (order placed, shipped, delivered), each sending an approved Utility template with an image header and tracking button. Shopify order and fulfilment webhooks fire the triggers. A status change you make in the dashboard enrols the journey directly, without waiting for Shopify.

items: Shopify connected with fulfilment permissions approved: [Connect Shopify](/docs/connect-shopify#permissions).
WhatsApp connected and sending.
Approved order-status templates, one per stage.

blocks.text: Which event maps to which trigger
There is **no "order confirmed" trigger**. An order being placed *is* the confirmation.
Shipping and delivery come from fulfilment events, so they need fulfilment permissions on the Shopify connection.

blocks.caption: Shopify event to journey trigger
rows: **Order placed**: use this for order confirmation
A fulfilment updates with a delivered shipment status
A fulfilment updates with any other status
You change the status in the TopEdge AI Orders screen
Shipped or out for delivery → **order shipped**; delivered → **order delivered**
Nothing sends: existing enrollments for that order are cancelled

blocks.title: Events that start an order journey
blocks.caption: A cancelled order cancels pending steps, so a customer never gets a shipping message for an order you already cancelled.

blocks.title: Dropped webhooks are retried
blocks.body: Webhooks occasionally fail to arrive. A reconcile job re-reads your orders on a schedule and fires anything missed, with a guard against sending the same update twice.

blocks.alt: Meta Manager template library with order-status templates and their approval status

Create one template per stage. The dashboard preview is exactly what the customer receives.

Courier name, tracking number and a working tracking link.
That it arrives today, and for COD the exact amount to keep ready.
Confirmation, plus one ask: a review, or a reorder link.

blocks.title: Keep order templates strictly transactional
blocks.body: One promotional word (sale, offer, discount, free gift) gets a Utility template rejected. To promote something, use a separate Marketing template sent to consented contacts.

blocks.text: Build the journeys

blocks.alt: Journeys hub listing the order lifecycle and cart automations

marks.label: On means the journey is sending

blocks.howToName: Automate Shopify order status updates on WhatsApp

steps.title: Start from the playbooks
steps.body: Open **Journeys** and click **Browse playbooks**. **Order placed**, **Order shipped** and **Order delivered** each create a journey with the right trigger and message step.
steps.alt: Browse playbooks dialog with the Order placed, Order shipped and Order delivered playbooks

steps.title: Map the approved template on each
steps.body: Open each journey, click **Edit settings** on the **Order status** step, and pick the approved template for that stage.

steps.title: Check the variable mapping
steps.body: Point each variable at an order field: order number, customer name, tracking URL. Unmapped variables send blanks.

steps.title: Decide on a delay
steps.body: Send the confirmation immediately. Delay the delivered message a few hours so it does not land while the customer is still at the door.

steps.title: Publish each journey
steps.body: Press **Publish** on one journey, test it, then move to the next. See [Turn a journey on or off](/docs/guides/turn-journeys-on-off).

steps.title: Test the full lifecycle
steps.body: Place a test order, then move it through shipped and delivered from the **Orders** screen. Each stage should send exactly one message.

items: A test order produces exactly one confirmation message.
Marking it shipped produces one shipping message with a working tracking link.
Marking it delivered produces one delivery message.
No stage sends twice when Shopify later echoes the same change.
Cancelling an order stops any pending status messages.

blocks.text: If order updates are not sending

cases.symptom: Order confirmations do not send
fixes: The journey uses the **order placed** trigger: there is no order confirmed trigger.
The journey is Published, not Draft.
The template shows Approved, and the order has a phone number in international format.
Read the skip reason on the order detail page: it names the exact cause.

cases.symptom: Shipped and delivered never fire, but confirmations work
fixes: Fulfilment permissions are missing. Settings → Shopify → **Reconnect** and approve everything.
Confirm the order is actually being fulfilled in Shopify, not just tagged.
If your courier updates by a 3PL feed rather than Shopify, check that integration is sending shipment status.

cases.symptom: A customer got the same update twice
fixes: Check you do not have two published journeys on the same trigger.
A manual status change plus a Shopify echo is de-duplicated per order and trigger, so duplicates almost always mean duplicate journeys.

cases.symptom: The message arrives with blank values
fixes: Variables are unmapped on the node: open it and map each one to an order field.
The field is genuinely empty on that order, such as a tracking number before dispatch.
Preview with a real order rather than sample data before publishing.

articles.title: Build a WhatsApp welcome menu with Flow Builder

articles.h1: How to build a welcome flow
articles.lead: Decide what customers see when they message you: a greeting, a menu, and a way to reach a person.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Flow Builder and Journeys?
faqs.answer: Flow Builder handles inbound conversations, what the bot says when a customer messages you, including menus, FAQ answers and handover to an agent. Journeys handle outbound automation triggered by Shopify events such as an order being placed or a cart being abandoned.

faqs.question: How many buttons can a WhatsApp message have?
faqs.answer: Three quick-reply buttons per message. If you need more options, use a list node instead, which presents up to ten rows behind a single tap and reads better than two stacked button messages.

faqs.question: Why does my flow still show the old menu after I edited it?
faqs.answer: Because the live bot runs a snapshot frozen at publish time. Saving the canvas updates the draft only. Publish again to replace the live graph, which takes effect from the next inbound message.

blocks.text: Open Flow Builder and start from the seeded welcome flow. Add a greeting with three or four buttons for your most common questions plus a live-chat handover, then test in the simulator and publish. Saving a draft changes nothing; publishing replaces the live graph from the next inbound message.

The hard part is choosing what to offer, not using the canvas.

items: **Read** the last fifty inbound messages in your inbox.
**Count** which questions repeat.
**Build** for the top four.
**Send** everything else to a human, never into a dead end.

rows: Look up the latest order and reply with its status and tracking link.
Answer directly, in two sentences, with a link.
Is this in stock / what size?
Answer if you can, otherwise hand to an agent.
I want to talk to someone
Hand over to Chats immediately: do not make them work for it.

articles.title: Send a WhatsApp broadcast that is Meta-safe
articles.description: Send a promotional WhatsApp broadcast to a consented segment: pick the audience, use an approved Marketing template, pass preflight, and read the results.
articles.h1: How to send a WhatsApp broadcast
articles.lead: Send one promotional message to a chosen group of customers who agreed to hear from you.

faqs.question: Do I need opt-in to send a WhatsApp broadcast?
faqs.answer: Yes. Promotional broadcasts use Marketing templates and require recorded consent from each contact. Transactional order updates are different: they send as Utility templates through journeys and do not need marketing consent.

faqs.question: Why was my broadcast blocked before sending?
faqs.answer: Preflight blocks a launch when too large a share of the audience has no recorded consent or has opted out. Fix the audience rather than the check: narrow to a consented segment, and remove any list you cannot prove consent for.

faqs.question: How many WhatsApp broadcasts can I send?
faqs.answer: Two separate limits apply. Your TopEdge AI plan caps campaign and email sends per billing cycle, and Meta caps how many unique customers you can start conversations with in 24 hours based on your quality rating and business verification.

blocks.text: Build a segment of contacts with recorded marketing consent and pick an approved **Marketing** template. Run the campaign preflight to catch opt-out and template problems, then send or schedule. Start with your smallest engaged segment, because your messaging limit and quality rating depend on how the first sends land.

items: An approved **Marketing** template: Utility templates cannot power broadcasts.
Contacts with recorded marketing consent: [Website opt-in](/docs/guides/website-opt-in).
A segment or CSV defining who receives it.
Enough send allowance left in the cycle: [limits](/docs/platform/limits-and-quotas).

blocks.title: Quality rating is the thing to protect
blocks.body: Blocks and reports lower your quality rating, and a low rating cuts how many customers you can message in 24 hours. One badly targeted broadcast can restrict your account for weeks.

blocks.text: Step 1, the audience, not the message

blocks.alt: Audience → Segments list with saved segments and their live matching counts

blocks.text: Decide who receives this before you write a word. A send to the 15% who bought in the last 90 days usually beats a send to everyone, in revenue and in account health.

rows: The default. Conditions on orders, spend, tags, consent and recency, with a live matching count.
When you want the most engaged contacts regardless of order history.
Only for lists you can attest consent for. The attestation is recorded against the import.
Small, deliberate sends: a VIP group, a restock waitlist.

blocks.text: Step 2, build and send

blocks.alt: Campaign builder on the audience and template step, with the recipient count

steps.title: Create the campaign
steps.body: **Campaigns → Create campaign**. Name it so you will recognise it in a results table later.

steps.title: Pick one channel
steps.body: WhatsApp or email, not both in one campaign. To do both, send two campaigns with audiences that do not overlap.

steps.title: Choose the audience
steps.body: Pick the segment. The count shown is the number of contacts who will actually receive it.

steps.title: Pick the Marketing template
steps.body: Only approved Marketing templates appear. Prefer name-only variables, since order variables render blank for contacts with no orders.

steps.title: Run preflight
steps.body: Preflight checks consent coverage and template readiness. It blocks a launch where too many contacts are opted out.
steps.note: A blocked preflight is doing you a favour. Fix the audience rather than looking for a way around it.

steps.title: Send or schedule
steps.body: Sends go out in paced batches, not all at once. That protects your account and your quality rating.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.body: Open the campaign row for sent, delivered, read and failed counts. It also shows revenue attributed to the campaign.

blocks.name: message-lifecycle
blocks.title: What the delivery numbers mean
blocks.caption: Delivered means it reached the phone. Read means they opened it. Failures are almost always an invalid number or a blocked contact.

blocks.text: Writing one that works

items: **Lead with the thing, not the greeting.** The first line is all most people read in a notification.
**One call to action.** Two links halve both.
**Say who you are.** On WhatsApp the sender is a phone number, not a logo. Name your store in the first line.
**Give them an exit.** An easy opt-out costs you a few contacts; a block costs you account health.
**Send during waking hours** in your customers’ timezone. A 2am notification earns a block.
Preflight passes with no consent blockers.
A test send to your own number renders correctly on a phone.
Variables resolve to real values, not blanks or dashes.
Delivered count is close to sent: a large gap means bad numbers.
Opt-outs after the send stay in single digits proportionally.

blocks.text: If a broadcast will not send

cases.symptom: Launch blocked, too many contacts opted out
fixes: Filter Audience by consent and look at who is excluded.
Remove any purchased or scraped list. There is no safe way to send to one.
Narrow to a consented segment and send to that instead.
For order updates, use a [journey](/docs/guides/order-status-updates) with a Utility template: no marketing consent needed.

cases.symptom: The template you want is not in the list
fixes: It is a Utility template. Broadcasts need the Marketing category.
It is still pending approval in Meta Manager.
Use **Sync from Meta** if it was approved outside TopEdge AI.

cases.symptom: Variables render as blanks or dashes
fixes: The template uses order variables but the segment has contacts with no orders.
Switch to a name-only template for broad sends.
Preview against a real contact before launching.

cases.symptom: Delivered is far below sent
fixes: Numbers are invalid or not on WhatsApp: clean the list.
Some recipients have blocked your number.
If it is widespread, check your quality rating in Meta Business Manager.

articles.description: Work a shared WhatsApp inbox: take a conversation over from the bot, reply inside and outside the 24-hour window, assign to a teammate and release it back.
articles.h1: How to reply to customers and take over from the bot
articles.lead: Answer a chat yourself, pause the bot while you do, and hand the conversation back when you are done.

faqs.question: Why can I not send a free-form WhatsApp reply?
faqs.answer: The customer has not messaged you in the last 24 hours, so the service window has closed. WhatsApp only allows approved templates outside that window. Once the customer replies to your template, free text works again for another 24 hours.

faqs.question: What happens to the bot when an agent takes over?
faqs.answer: It pauses for that conversation only, and other conversations keep running their flows. It stays paused until someone presses **Give back to bot** or **Mark as done**, which is why a thread that seems permanently silent is usually still paused.

faqs.question: Can several agents work the same WhatsApp number?
faqs.answer: Yes. That is the point of a shared inbox: one business number, many agents, with assignment so two people do not answer the same customer. Each reply is attributed to the agent who sent it.

blocks.text: Open a conversation in Chats and press **Reply myself**; the bot pauses so only your team replies. Within 24 hours of the customer’s last message you can send free text, and after that you must pick an approved template. Press **Mark as done** or **Give back to bot** when you finish, and automation resumes on the next inbound message.

articles.title: Collect WhatsApp opt-in on your storefront
articles.description: Add a popup, spin wheel or WhatsApp widget to your Shopify store, write consent wording that holds up, and confirm leads land in Audience.
articles.h1: How to collect WhatsApp opt-ins on your store
articles.lead: Add a popup, spin wheel or chat widget to your store so visitors can agree to WhatsApp messages.

faqs.question: What counts as valid WhatsApp marketing opt-in?
faqs.answer: A clear, affirmative action by the customer, with wording beside it that names WhatsApp marketing from your store specifically. A pre-ticked box, a buried line in your terms, or a list you bought do not count, and relying on them puts your business number at risk.

faqs.question: Why is my opt-in popup not showing on my Shopify store?
faqs.answer: In order of likelihood: the tool is still a draft, the TopEdge AI app embed is not enabled on your live theme, an ad blocker is hiding it, or your display rules exclude the page you are testing on. Test in an incognito window with blockers off.

faqs.question: Do customers have to opt in again to receive order updates?
faqs.answer: No. Order, shipping and delivery updates are transactional and send as Utility templates, which do not require marketing consent. Opt-in governs promotional broadcasts only, and opting out of marketing does not stop order updates.

blocks.text: Create a popup, spin wheel or WhatsApp widget in **Opt-in tools**, with consent wording that names WhatsApp marketing. Publish it, then enable the TopEdge AI opt-in app embed on your **live** Shopify theme. Each submission lands in Audience with its consent source recorded.

items: Shopify connected.
WhatsApp connected, for the widget and for messaging those contacts later.
Theme editor access in Shopify admin.
A test phone number you can submit.

blocks.text: Pick the right tool

blocks.alt: Opt-in tools hub listing popups, spin wheels and the WhatsApp widget with their status

Scratch or tap to reveal. Similar to the spin wheel, lighter visually.
A launcher that opens a chat with your number. The customer messages you first, which both captures them and opens the 24-hour window.

blocks.title: The widget is the quietest high performer
blocks.body: A customer who starts the chat gives you the strongest signal, and their first message opens the 24-hour window. Nobody has to dismiss it, so it never annoys anyone.

steps.title: Create the tool

steps.title: Design it and write the consent line

steps.body: **Shopify admin → Online Store → Themes → Customize** on the **live** theme → **App embeds** → enable **TopEdge AI Opt-In** → **Save**.
steps.note: No theme file editing is needed, and nothing is left behind if you disable it.

steps.body: Open your store in a private window, wait out the delay, and submit your real phone number. Hard-refresh if you just published.

steps.title: Confirm the contact landed
steps.body: Open **All customers**. The contact should appear within a minute or two with marketing consent recorded.

A customer who replies **STOP** or **UNSUBSCRIBE** is opted out of WhatsApp marketing immediately. Hindi and Hinglish replies such as **BAND**, **BAND KARO**, **MAT BHEJO** and **बंद करो** work too.
The reply must be the keyword on its own, and you do not need to do anything. No promotional message reaches them again unless they reply **START** or **SUBSCRIBE**; order updates still send.

blocks.body: Messaging numbers that never opted in produces blocks and reports, which lower your WhatsApp quality rating and cut your messaging limit. The damage lands on your business number and takes weeks to recover from.

articles.title: Train the AI to answer customer questions
articles.description: Add your own AI key, load store knowledge, train intents on real customer phrases, and test confidence before letting the AI reply to customers.
articles.h1: How to train the AI to answer customers
articles.lead: Teach the AI your store’s facts and the way your customers really ask questions.

faqs.question: Do I need my own OpenAI or Gemini key?
faqs.answer: For AI-generated replies, yes. TopEdge AI uses your own key, so usage is billed to you by that provider and you keep control of which model answers your customers. Keyword-matched intents with fixed replies work without any key.

faqs.question: How many example phrases does an intent need?
faqs.answer: Five to ten, taken from real customer messages rather than written by you. Phrases in your own phrasing score poorly because customers do not write like the person who built the store: expect Hinglish, abbreviations and no punctuation.

faqs.question: Should the AI handle refunds and complaints?
faqs.answer: No. Route anything involving money, a complaint or a legal question to a human. A confidently wrong answer about a refund costs far more than the time it saved, and customers escalate it publicly.

blocks.text: Add your own Gemini or OpenAI key and fill in store knowledge: shipping, returns, sizing and payment. Then create intents with five to ten phrases each, written the way customers actually type. Test each intent's confidence and activate it, because an inactive intent never matches.

items: WhatsApp connected, for live replies.
A Gemini or OpenAI API key. Keyword-only intents work without one.
A published flow as the fallback router: [Build your first flow](/docs/guides/build-your-first-flow).
Fifty real inbound messages to read before you start writing phrases.

blocks.title: You bring your own key
blocks.body: The AI runs on your own Gemini or OpenAI key, so the provider bills you for usage and you are not locked to a model TopEdge AI picked. Add it under **AI & API key**.

blocks.text: Step 1, load the knowledge

blocks.alt: AI & API key with the store knowledge fields for shipping, returns, payments and sizing

blocks.text: The AI cannot invent your return window, and it should not try. Fill in store knowledge before any intent work, because it grounds every generated answer.

items: **Shipping**: dispatch time, delivery time by region, courier partners, what happens to a delayed order.
**Returns and exchanges**: the window, the condition requirement, who pays return shipping, how refunds are issued.
**Payments**: which methods you accept, whether COD is available and where, any COD fee.
**Sizing and product care**: the questions your category always gets.
**What you do not do**: no international shipping, no exchanges on sale items. Knowing the limits stops invented answers.

blocks.text: Step 2, set the persona
**AI & API key → Bot personality** sets the assistant’s name and tone. Keep it plain and close to how your brand already writes.
A wacky persona ages badly and makes complaints read worse than they are.
Step 3, train intents on real phrases

blocks.alt: Audience → Intent list with each intent's phrases and Active toggle

steps.title: Read your inbox first
steps.body: Open the last fifty inbound messages and group them. The groups are your intents; the messages are your phrases.

steps.title: Create the intent
steps.body: **Audience → Intent → Add intent**. Name it for the question, such as "Shipping time".

steps.title: Add five to ten real phrases
steps.body: Copy how customers actually write: Hinglish, abbreviations, typos, no punctuation. "kitne din me ayega" trains better than "What is your delivery time?".
steps.note: Phrases you invented yourself are the main cause of low confidence scores.

steps.title: Choose what it does
steps.body: Reply with text, start a flow, assign to an agent, or escalate. Route asks like "I want a refund" to a human, not the AI.

steps.title: Activate it
steps.body: Toggle **Active**. An inactive intent never matches in production, however well trained.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Type sample messages into the test tool and read the matched intent and its confidence. Low or wrong matches need more phrases, or a split intent.

blocks.caption: Reading the test results
rows: Add three to five more phrases closer to how the message was worded.
Two intents are competing. Split them into narrower ones, or deactivate the duplicate.
Expected for genuinely new questions. Make sure your flow fallback hands these to a human.

blocks.title: Escalation is a feature, not a failure
blocks.body: The most damaging AI reply is a confident wrong one about a refund or a delivery date. Route money, complaints and anything legal to a human by design.

items: Your AI key is saved and the knowledge tabs accept input.
The test tool matches your sample phrases to the right intents.
Each intent you want live is toggled **Active**.
A real inbound message gets an AI reply when the bot is not paused on that thread.
An escalation intent puts the thread in the agent queue.

blocks.text: If the AI answers badly

cases.symptom: Test matches the wrong intent or reports low confidence
fixes: Add three to five more phrases in customers’ own words.
Split broad intents: "Shipping" and "Returns" should not be one intent.
Deactivate duplicate intents competing for the same phrases.

cases.symptom: The AI answers but the facts are wrong
fixes: Fill the gap in store knowledge: an empty field is where invention happens.
Add the limits explicitly, including what you do **not** offer.
Change that intent to a fixed reply instead of a generated one.

cases.symptom: The AI never replies at all
fixes: Check the intents are Active.
Check no agent pressed **Reply myself** on the thread in Chats.
Confirm your AI key is saved and valid with its provider.
Confirm a flow is Published as the fallback router.

articles.title: Run digital warranty registration on WhatsApp
articles.description: Set up warranty batches, share a mobile registration portal with WhatsApp OTP, and move claims through approved, shipped or rejected with automatic updates.
articles.h1: How to set up warranty registration
articles.lead: Let customers register a product on WhatsApp by scanning a QR code on the box.

faqs.question: How do customers register a warranty?
faqs.answer: They open your public registration portal, usually by scanning a QR on the packaging, select their product, enter their phone number and verify it with a WhatsApp OTP. The registration is then matched against the Shopify order where one exists.

faqs.question: Do customers need an account to claim?
faqs.answer: No. Registration and claims both work from a mobile web page with WhatsApp OTP verification, so there is no password and no app to install. That is deliberate: every extra step loses registrations.

blocks.text: Create a warranty batch linking Shopify products to coverage dates, then share the public registration portal, where customers verify by WhatsApp OTP. Work claims through pending, approved, shipped or rejected. Each status change sends the customer a WhatsApp update automatically.

items: Shopify connected: batches link to products and registrations match against orders.
WhatsApp connected: the registration OTP and every claim update send over WhatsApp.
A plan that includes the warranty module.
A test product and a phone you can receive an OTP on.

articles.title: Segment Shopify customers for WhatsApp
articles.description: Build dynamic customer segments from order history, spend, tags and consent, then launch a WhatsApp or email campaign straight from the segment.
articles.h1: How to build a customer segment
articles.lead: Group customers by what they bought and when, so each campaign goes to the people likely to buy.

faqs.question: Are TopEdge AI segments dynamic or a fixed list?
faqs.answer: Dynamic. A saved segment re-evaluates its conditions, so contacts move in and out as they order, lapse or change consent. You build a segment like "lapsed 90 days" once and it stays correct without any maintenance.

faqs.question: Why does my segment match zero customers?
faqs.answer: Conditions combine with AND, so every rule has to be true at once. Two reasonable-looking rules, say, more than three orders and ordered in the last seven days, can easily describe nobody. Add conditions one at a time and watch the live count.

blocks.text: Build a segment in **Audience → Customer groups** by stacking conditions on order count, spend, tags, consent and recency, and watch the live matching count. Save it, then press **Launch campaign** to open the broadcast builder with that audience selected.

items: Shopify connected, so order history and spend are populated.
Contacts in Audience: from [opt-in tools](/docs/guides/website-opt-in), checkout consent or orders.
Marketing consent recorded, if the segment will receive promotional messages.

blocks.text: Segments worth building first

rows: Cross-sell the obvious companion product, or ask for a review.
Two or more orders, consent recorded
Early access and restocks. This is your most valuable list.
A genuine reason to come back. This is where a discount earns its keep.
Treat differently: human outreach often beats a broadcast here.
Safe to push harder. These customers never cost you RTO.
Nothing promotional. Consider requiring prepayment instead.

blocks.text: Build a segment

blocks.alt: Audience → Segments list with saved segments and their live matching counts

blocks.howToName: Build a customer segment for a WhatsApp campaign

steps.title: Open the segment builder
steps.body: **Audience → Customer groups**. Name it for what it is, like "Repeat buyers, consented".

steps.title: Stack your conditions
steps.body: Add conditions on order count, total spend, tags, consent, days since last purchase or RTO count. They combine with AND.
steps.note: Because it is AND, three conditions can easily match nobody. Add one at a time and watch the count.

steps.title: Watch the matching count
steps.body: It updates as you edit. Zero means your conditions are too strict, so remove the last one you added.

steps.title: Include consent if you will market to it
steps.body: Without a consent condition, campaign preflight trims the audience anyway. Adding it here makes the count you see the count that sends.

steps.title: Save it
steps.body: Saved segments are dynamic: contacts move in and out as their behaviour changes. You never rebuild them.

steps.title: Launch a campaign from it
steps.body: Press **Launch campaign** to open the broadcast builder with this audience selected. See [Send a broadcast](/docs/guides/whatsapp-broadcast).

blocks.text: Lead scores, when order history is not enough
Lead scores rank contacts by engagement, not purchases, using waterfall rules you define. They surface contacts who opted in and browsed but never ordered, a group order-history segments cannot see.

blocks.title: Phone numbers match with or without the country code
blocks.body: Audience search handles Indian numbers both ways, so you do not have to guess the format a contact was saved in. Messages still send in full international format.

items: The segment’s matching count is a plausible number, not zero.
Spot-check three contacts: they genuinely meet the conditions.
A consent condition is present if the segment will be marketed to.
**Launch campaign** opens the builder with the segment selected.
The campaign audience count matches the segment count.

blocks.text: If a segment looks wrong

cases.symptom: Matching count is zero
fixes: Conditions combine with AND: remove the most recently added one.
Check a date condition is not set to a window with no orders in it.
Confirm orders have actually synced from Shopify.

cases.symptom: The campaign audience is smaller than the segment
fixes: Contacts without marketing consent are excluded at send time.
Contacts who replied STOP are permanently excluded from marketing.
Add a consent condition to the segment so the two counts agree.

cases.symptom: A contact you expected is missing
fixes: Search by their number both with and without the country code.
Check they are not excluded by a consent or tag condition.
If they just opted in, allow a minute or two and refresh.

articles.title: Journeys reference: triggers, nodes, publishing
articles.description: Complete reference for TopEdge AI Journeys, every trigger type, trigger filter, node type, wait behaviour, publishing rule and revenue attribution window.
articles.lead: Journeys send messages on their own when something happens in your store: an order, a shipment, an abandoned cart.

faqs.question: Why is my published journey not sending?
faqs.answer: Check in this order: the journey shows **Live**, each step’s template reads **Approved**, the conditions on the Entry step do not exclude the customer, and the customer has a phone number. The order’s activity list names the exact reason a message was skipped.

faqs.question: Do conditions combine with AND or OR?
faqs.answer: Always AND. Every condition must be true for a customer to enter, which is why two reasonable conditions together can leave nobody.

faqs.question: How is revenue credited to a journey?
faqs.answer: If a journey message was the last TopEdge AI message a customer got in the 7 days before ordering, that journey gets the credit. They do not need to tap the link.

blocks.text: A journey sends messages on its own when something happens in your store. It has one trigger, the steps that follow, and a **Live** switch. Nothing sends until you press **Publish**.
How a journey runs
When the trigger happens, the customer enters the journey and each of their steps is scheduled. If they reply, their remaining steps are cancelled. That is on by default.

blocks.name: journey-runtime
blocks.title: From Shopify event to sent message
blocks.caption: When a send does not happen, the skip reason on the order names which stage stopped it.

blocks.title: Edits need a second Publish
blocks.body: Saving keeps a draft. Customers keep getting the published version, trigger included, until you press **Publish** again.

blocks.text: Triggers
The trigger is set on the **Entry** step, under **When**.

rows: A new order arrives from Shopify. Use it for order confirmation and COD confirmation.
An order is fulfilled, or its shipment updates.
A shopper leaves checkout after typing a phone number, once your wait time has passed.
A shopper whose phone number you already have looks at a product or page.
Someone signs up through one of your [opt-in tools](/docs/reference/opt-in-tools).

blocks.title: There is no "order confirmed" trigger
blocks.body: An order being placed is the confirmation. Use **Order placed**.

blocks.text: When a customer leaves early

items: **Customer replies**: on by default, so nobody is chased after they answer.
**Order cancelled**: on the order triggers.

blocks.text: Conditions: who enters
On the **Entry** step, **Add condition** narrows who enters. **Every condition must be true**, so two narrow conditions together can leave nobody.

rows: COD only. This is how a COD confirmation journey skips prepaid orders.
Only orders with a certain product, or without it.
Include or exclude orders by tag.
Only orders going to certain places.
Only orders that used a certain code.
blocks.caption: Conditions on order triggers

rows: How long after the shopper leaves before the first reminder. 25 minutes by default, 5 minutes at least.
Skip small carts that are not worth a message.
blocks.caption: Settings on the cart abandoned trigger

blocks.text: Only carts with a phone number enter a cart journey.
Steps you can add

blocks.alt: Journey builder with three cart reminders and the waits between them, and the list of steps on the right

blocks.text: Add steps from the **Steps** panel on the right: drag one onto the canvas, or tap **+**.

rows: Sends an email from your connected Gmail.
Sends a payment link so a COD customer can pay now. Growth plan and above.
Asks a COD customer to confirm or cancel with one tap.
A cart reminder with the product image and a button back to checkout. Can add a cart discount or a matching email.
The update for one stage of an order: confirmed, shipped or delivered.
Hands the customer to a published flow from [Flow Builder](/docs/reference/flow-builder).
Splits customers into two paths by a rule, such as whether they replied. Growth plan and above.
Sends two versions to compare which one works better.

faqs.answer: In order of likelihood: the journey is still in Draft rather than Published, the template it uses is not Approved at send time, trigger filters are excluding the customer, or the order has no phone number. articles.h1: How to turn a journey on or off
articles.lead: A journey only sends once it is published. Here is how to switch one on, check it is running and stop it.

faqs.question: Why is my journey not sending anything?
faqs.answer: Most often it is still a Draft. Saving a draft does not publish it. Open the journey and press **Publish**, then check the row shows **Live** on the Journeys screen.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Draft and Live?
faqs.answer: A Draft is a journey you are still building. It never sends. A Live journey is published and messages every customer who matches its trigger.

faqs.question: Do I lose my journey if I switch it off?
faqs.answer: No. The steps, templates and results stay as they are. Switch it back on when you are ready.

blocks.text: Open the journey from **Journeys** and press **Publish**. Its status changes from **Draft** to **Live** and it starts sending on the next matching event. To stop it, switch off **Live** on its row.
Read the status first

steps.body: In the sidebar click **Journeys**, then click the journey’s name.

steps.title: Check every message step has a template
steps.body: Click **Edit settings** on each message step. A step with no approved template cannot send.

steps.title: Press Publish

articles.h1: How to create a WhatsApp template
articles.lead: Write a message once, send it to Meta for approval, then use it in any journey or campaign.

faqs.question: How long does Meta take to approve a template?
faqs.answer: Often a few minutes, and usually within a day. Meta does not promise a time. The status in Meta Manager changes to **Approved** on its own.

faqs.question: Why was my template rejected?
faqs.answer: The usual reason is the wrong category: a promotional word such as sale, offer or discount inside a Utility template. Move the promotion to a Marketing template, or remove the word, and submit again.

faqs.question: Can I edit a template after it is approved?
faqs.answer: Editing sends it back to Meta for review, and it cannot send while in review. For a big change, create a new template and switch your journey to it once approved.

blocks.text: Open **Meta Manager** and click **Create Meta template**. Give it a name, choose the category, write the message and press **Submit for review**. You can use it once its status reads **Approved**.

items: WhatsApp is connected: [Connect WhatsApp](/docs/connect-whatsapp).
You know what the message is for: an order update, or a promotion.

blocks.title: Check the blueprints first
blocks.body: The **Blueprints** tab has ready-made sets for order updates and cart recovery, with the image, variables and button already filled in. Start there if one fits.

blocks.text: Create the template

blocks.howToName: Create a WhatsApp message template in TopEdge AI

steps.title: Open Meta Manager
steps.body: In the sidebar click **Meta Manager**, then **Create Meta template** at the top right.
steps.alt: WhatsApp templates list with the Create Meta template button at the top right

steps.title: Name it
steps.body: **Template name** is for you, for example "Order confirmed". **Meta template name** is how Meta files it: lowercase with underscores, like `order_confirmed`.
steps.alt: New WhatsApp template form with template name, Meta template name, category, language, header and body fields

marks.label: Two names: yours, and the one Meta files it under

steps.title: Choose the category
steps.body: Pick **Utility** for messages about an order the customer already placed. Pick **Marketing** for offers, launches and reminders to buy.
steps.note: The form starts on Marketing. Change it for order updates, or Meta charges and reviews the message as marketing.

steps.title: Add a header if you want one
steps.body: Under **Header** choose **Text**, **Image**, **Video** or **Document**. A product image works well for order and cart messages. **None** is fine too.

steps.title: Write the body
steps.body: Type the message. Where a detail changes per customer, click **+ Add variable**. It shows as `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` and is filled with the name, order number or amount when the message sends.

steps.title: Add buttons
steps.body: Under **Buttons** click **Add button**. Use a link button such as "Track order", or quick replies such as "Confirm" and "Cancel".

steps.title: Check the preview and submit
steps.body: The preview on the right is exactly what the customer will see. Press **Submit for review**. To finish later, press **Save draft**.

rows: Ready. Pick it in a journey or campaign.
Open it, fix the wording or category, and submit again.

blocks.text: Utility or Marketing?

rows: Order confirmed, shipped, delivered, COD confirmation
Offers, new arrivals, cart reminders with a discount, win-back

blocks.title: One promotional word can reject a Utility template
blocks.body: Words like sale, offer, discount or free gift make Meta treat the message as marketing. Keep order messages about the order.

cases.symptom: The template was rejected
fixes: Remove promotional wording from a Utility template, or change the category to Marketing.
Make sure every variable has ordinary words around it. A message that is only variables is rejected.
Do not start or end the body with a variable.

cases.symptom: The approved template does not appear in a journey
fixes: Press **Sync from Meta** on the step’s template picker.
Check the template was created on the same WhatsApp account that is connected in Settings.
